permutationLabel: Typed complaint, bleeding frame (colour, relation to stool)
summary: 32-year-old woman: 2 months of bright red blood on the toilet paper after straining, separate from the stool; no change in bowel habit or weight loss.

inputs.hpi: Two months of bright red blood on the toilet paper after passing hard stools, sometimes drips into the pan. Separate from the stool. Painless. No change in bowel habit, no mucus, no weight loss. No family history of bowel cancer.

exam.other: PR normal. Proctoscopy: grade I internal haemorrhoids.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: First-degree internal haemorrhoids
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Outlet-type bleeding from grade I haemorrhoids.

rationale: The bleeding frame asks the colour and where the blood is (on the paper, in the pan, mixed with stool) — the outlet pattern of haemorrhoids — not SOCRATES pain questions.
